title: ffmpeg CLI deadlocks at EOF when encoding filtergraph video + audio in one process - encoder's delayed frames never flushed
body:
# Summary of the bug
ffmpeg cli hands forever in this specific circumstance

reproducible on current master (N-122509 built 2026-07-09). Hands forever on 00:00:04.94

Fair warning - following is output from a LLM, but it seems plausible to me:
```
A single ffmpeg invocation that encodes BOTH a filtergraph video output (libx264)
and a filtergraph audio output (aac) can deadlock at end-of-stream. The filtergraph
completes every frame, demuxer/decoder threads terminate normally, the sync queue
records EOF — but the frames still buffered inside the video encoder are never
flushed. The process stays alive forever, emitting -progress blocks with a static
frame counter and speed decaying toward 0x. The output file never gets its trailer.

The frozen frame count always equals total_frames − encoder_delay:
  * threads=30 (auto), rc-lookahead=10, bf=3  -> stuck at 105 of 151
  * -threads 1                                 -> stuck at 138 (delay 13)
  * sliced-threads, rc-lookahead=0, bf=0       -> stuck at 148

It is a race: with the attached repro (~14 inputs, 3840x2160) it triggers in
roughly 1 in 4–8 runs (verified on both the 2026-04-30 build and current master);
with our original production graph (21 inputs) roughly 3 in 5. Running two
instances concurrently raises the odds. Lower resolutions reproduce much more
rarely (narrower window). Note: adding -v debug lowers the repro rate further
(timing-sensitive), which is why the attached debug log is from the production
graph — the stall signature is identical.

What we ruled out
-----------------
* Video-only (identical graph with the audio chains removed): NEVER hangs (0/6).
  Filtergraph audio in the same process is a required ingredient.
* Removing -shortest: still hangs.
* Removing -filter_buffered_frames: still hangs.
* Encoder thread count / delay knobs: only move the frozen frame number.
* Not build-specific: reproduced on BtbN win64-gpl autobuilds
  N-124278-gcc3ca17127-20260430, N-125365-g9a01c1cb6a-20260630, and
  N-125509-g8ad6288553-20260709 (current master at time of filing).

Environment
-----------
Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, 20 logical cores, 64 GB RAM.
BtbN FFmpeg-Builds win64-gpl (exact -version banners can be provided for all three).
(Not yet verified on Linux; the repro script is POSIX sh and should run anywhere.)

Reproduction
------------
The attached repro.sh first GENERATES all inputs with ffmpeg itself (a video-only
background mp4, five small mov files with h264+aac, one png), then loops the
deadlocking command 10 times. On affected builds at least one iteration wedges:
ffmpeg stops writing output at frame=105/151 but keeps emitting -progress blocks
(speed decays toward 0.00x) and never exits.

-v debug observations from a hung run (log attached)
----------------------------------------------------
* Every overlay logs its final frame (n:151 t:5.0) — the graph fully completed.
* [out#0/mp4] "sq: 0 EOF" and "sq: finish 0; head ts 5" are logged.
* All decoder/demuxer threads log "Terminating thread with return code 0" and
  "All consumers of this stream are done".
* After that: nothing. No libx264 flush output, no trailer write. The remaining
  ~46 frames (encoder delay at threads=30+lookahead10+bf3) are never drained.
* Audio had already finished muxing (out_time in the progress stream sits at the
  AAC end ≈ 4.949s) while video packets stop at ~3.5s (105 frames).
```

# Steps to reproduce

Run the repro.sh in a dedicated directory to observe repro.

title: avutil/hwcontext_vulkan: query the actual image format in try_export_flags
body:
GetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2() must be queried with the format
that will actually be used to create the image, otherwise the external
memory export capability check answers for a different format than the one
being allocated.

When AV_VK_FRAME_FLAG_DISABLE_MULTIPLANE is set (e.g. by ffplay for CUDA
interop), vulkan_frames_init selects the per-plane fallback format via
vkfmt_from_pixfmt2(disable_multiplane=1) and stores it in hwctx->format[].
The image is then created with that fallback format. Querying the
multiplane vkf instead returns capability for a format that is never
instantiated, and on NVIDIA GPUs with OPTIMAL tiling the answer differs
between the two formats, producing broken CUDA hwaccel output.

Read hwctx->format[0], which is populated by vulkan_frames_init before
vulkan_pool_alloc runs, so the query matches the image regardless of
whether the multiplane or fallback path was taken.

Fix artifacts with `ffplay -hwaccel cuda foo.mp4`.

-------------------------------

`ffplay -hwaccel cuda` was broken since d5f4a55123393756c3a3e75cc8, but d5f4a55123393756c3a3e75cc8 isn't the root cause.

title: libavcodec/libzvbi-teletextdec.c: Support colored subtitles in SubRip output
body:
DVB teletext subtitles use color to differentiate between speakers.

When extracting these subtitles to SubRip format, FFmpeg (via libzvbi)
strips out all color information, resulting in plain-text output and white
text on screen.

Media players including VLC, mpv and Kodi will render SubRip subtitles in
color if HTML <font color="..."> tags are present.

While FFmpeg supports colored subtitles via the Advanced SubStation Alpha
format, support for this format is not universal and can add unnecessary
overhead when rendering.

# Summary of changes

This patch introduces a new -txt_format option named text_color, which
extracts DVB teletext subtitles to SubRip format with color information
retained.

title: arnndn emits exactly 480 NaN samples per channel at end of stream
body:
Component: avfilter · Keywords: arnndn NaN
Summary: af_arnndn: partial final frame at EOS is processed past its valid samples, emitting a full frame of NaNs (aac encode then fails with "Input contains (near) NaN/+-Inf")

Description
-------------
When the input stream's total sample count is not a multiple of 480 (the RNNoise frame size), arnndn emits exactly 480 NaN samples per channel at end of stream. If the output feeds an encoder that validates its input (e.g. the native aac encoder), the whole encode fails at flush:

[aac @ ...] Input contains (near) NaN/+-Inf
[aost#0:0/aac @ ...] [enc:aac @ ...] Error submitting audio frame to the encoder
[aost#0:0/aac @ ...] [enc:aac @ ...] Error flushing encoder: Invalid argument
[aost#0:0/aac @ ...] Task finished with error code: -22 (Invalid argument)
[aac @ ...] 2 frames left in the queue on closing
Conversion failed!

Reproduce
------------
Any RNNoise model file works (below: bd.rnnn from the rnnoise-models collection). The only requirement is an input whose length is NOT a whole number of 480-sample frames.
Fails (30.005 s @ 48 kHz = 1440240 samples = 3000.5 frames):
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=30.005" -af "arnndn=m=bd.rnnn,astats" -f null -
...
[Parsed_astats_1 @ ...] Number of NaNs: 480
Same command with duration=30.000 (exactly 3000 frames) reports Number of NaNs: 0.
With an aac sink instead of astats/null, the NaN frame aborts the encode with the log quoted above.
Reproduced with ffmpeg version 2026-07-06-git-c6498178bb-full_build-www.gyan.dev (Windows, gcc 16.1.0) and the defect is visible in current master source. Note the out-of-bounds read itself is much older: a 2022 build (2022-08-25-git-9bf9d42d01) processes the same partial frame and also outputs the padded 1440480 samples, but the garbage happened to stay finite there, so it went unnoticed.

Analysis
---------
In libavfilter/af_arnndn.c, activate() requests exact full frames:
ret = ff_inlink_consume_samples(inlink, FRAME_SIZE, FRAME_SIZE, &in);
At EOS the framework delivers the remaining partial frame anyway (observed: for a 1440240-sample input the filter outputs 1440480 samples, i.e. the tail frame is emitted at full size). filter_frame() then processes a full FRAME_SIZE frame unconditionally:
out = ff_get_audio_buffer(outlink, FRAME_SIZE);
...
ff_filter_execute(ctx, rnnoise_channels, &td, NULL, ...);
rnnoise_channel() reads FRAME_SIZE input samples with no in->nb_samples check, i.e. it reads past the valid samples of the partial frame into uninitialized buffer memory. The FFT window mixes the whole frame, so one bad tail value poisons all 480 output samples — matching the observed "Number of NaNs: 480" exactly.

Expected behavior: the final partial frame should be zero-padded to FRAME_SIZE before processing (and/or the output trimmed to in->nb_samples), never read past nb_samples.

Workaround: insert asetnsamples=n=480:p=1 before arnndn so no partial frame reaches the filter.

title: avformat/hlsenc: Fix three security‑related implementation detail issues
body:
## Security Fixes for HLS Module

### 1. `avformat/hlsenc: Fix heap buffer overflow in parse_playlist()`
- **Issue**: When parsing `IV=0x...` and `URI="..."` tokens, `av_strlcpy()` used `end - ptr` as the destination size instead of the actual buffer size. A crafted playlist with IV/URI tokens longer than 33 bytes could overflow into adjacent heap data.
- **Fix**: Use `FFMIN(end - ptr + 1, sizeof(buf))` to cap the copy size to the actual destination buffer.

### 2. `avformat/hls: Enforce protocol checks when opening child playlists`
- **Issue**: When parsing a master playlist, the demuxer called `c->ctx->io_open()` directly for child playlists, bypassing the `open_url()` helper that enforces protocol whitelisting (file/http/data) and file extension checks.
- **Fix**: Route the `!in` branch through `open_url()` so all child playlists are subject to the same security policy as segment URLs.

### 3. `avformat/hlsenc: Handle extensionless URIs in extract_segment_number()`
- **Issue**: `extract_segment_number()` called `strrchr(filename, '.')` and immediately did `dot - 1` without NULL check. A segment URI without an extension caused undefined behavior (NULL pointer arithmetic).
- **Fix**: Add NULL check and return -1 early when no dot is found.

title: avutil/hwcontext_vulkan: declare cuda as a transfer-compatible format
body:
The cuda hwcontext has listed AV_PIX_FMT_VULKAN among its supported
formats since Vulkan interop was first added, so a device's frame
constraints advertise Vulkan as a transfer-compatible ("sw") format.
This is what allows an hwupload targeting a cuda device to accept a
Vulkan frame as input during format negotiation.

The Vulkan hwcontext never made the reciprocal declaration, so an
hwupload targeting a Vulkan device would not accept a cuda frame, and a
cuda -> Vulkan upload could not be configured even though the transfer
itself is supported. Advertise AV_PIX_FMT_CUDA in the Vulkan frame
constraints to ensure we have consistent behaviour in both directions.

title: Fix d3d12va bitstream size checking
body:
D3D12VA fully trusts the return value of ff_d3d12va_get_suitable_max_bitstream_size(), which just returns av_image_get_buffer_size(frames_ctx->sw_format, avctx->coded_width, avctx->coded_height, 1).
No size checking was done.
So a file specifically crafted to bust that limit is able to overflow that buffer.
At least I wasn't able to find any size checking done anywhere, so this is what this series adds.

This was originally found by depthfirst, but only the instance the first commit fixes.
When I looked into it more, I found the same issue in all other d3d12va decoders, as well as the other instance inside of the AV1 one.

title: avfilter/vf_scale_cuda: improve generic filtering and Lanczos quality
body:
This PR fixes single-axis scaling through the existing generic weight-LUT path and improves the quality of Lanczos scaling in `scale_cuda`.

The generic path previously ran an empty horizontal intermediate pass when only one dimension changed, producing an all-zero frame. The intermediate pass is now allocated and executed only when temporary filter weights exist.

Lanczos now uses the existing generic separable filter path by default. This:

- Generates normalized Lanczos weights through libswscale.
- Widens the filter when downscaling for proper anti-aliasing.
- Supports a configurable radius from 1 to 10 through `param`.
- Uses a floating-point intermediate for two-axis scaling to avoid quantization between the horizontal and vertical passes.
- Saturates and rounds generic output to the input format's valid code range while preserving MSB alignment.

The legacy four-tap Lanczos implementation remains available with `use_filters=0`. The `scale_cuda` documentation is updated accordingly.

No public API or ABI changes are introduced.

No new FATE samples are included because these paths require CUDA
hardware.

title: Regression in FFmpeg 8.1: scale_cuda=format=yuv420p produces a completely green output when using hevc_nvenc.
body:
#Summary

Regression in FFmpeg 8.1: scale_cuda=format=yuv420p produces a completely green output when using hevc_nvenc.

#Working version

FFmpeg 7.1

#Broken version

FFmpeg 8.1

#Command

ffmpeg -hwaccel cuda -hwaccel_output_format cuda -i input.mkv \
-vf "scale_cuda=format=yuv420p" \
-c:v hevc_nvenc -preset p7 -profile:v main \
-rc constqp -qp 35 -rc-lookahead 58 \
-multipass fullres -aq-strength 5 \
-spatial-aq 1 -nonref_p 1 \
-an -sn -map_metadata -1 output.mkv

#Expected result

Correct HEVC output.

#Actual result

The encoded video consists entirely of a green image.

Removing the scale_cuda=format=yuv420p filter immediately fixes the problem, using otherwise identical encoding settings.

The same command works correctly with FFmpeg 7.1.
